title: Share and Tell
summary: A Windows file server shares a folder with everyone, and the folder tells you more than it should. From a staff account to the local administrator is one reused password away.
story: Pinecone Logistics (made up) runs a Windows server, WIN-FS01, on 10.10.3.0/24. You start on scout, a Linux box on the same network. Nobody has given you an account.
goal: Capture the user flag on a staff member's desktop and the administrator flag on the Administrator desktop.
skills: SMB shares, null sessions, winrm-shell, finding credentials in files, local administrator

hints.text: Scan 10.10.3.0/24, then 10.10.3.40. Port 445 is Windows file sharing. List its shares with no account: smbclient -L //10.10.3.40 -N
The Public share allows anonymous access (smbclient //10.10.3.40/Public -N). Read every file: one is a note to new staff with a password.
winrm-shell -i 10.10.3.40 -u kim -p PASSWORD gives a PowerShell session. Look in kim's Documents for an IT script: it has the local administrator password. Sign in again as Administrator.
